subject: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production
messages:
From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@pulseai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:12:03 -0800
Subject: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing intermittent high latency and truncated chunks on our live chat embedding since ~07:40 PST this morning. Users experience a stall of 6-20s mid-stream and then either a large jump of tokens or a reconnect. This is affecting our root chat flow in the mobile app.

I attached a short snippet of the client logs and a few request IDs. Example request id: req_77b2f1a4.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something in our integration? We currently use streaming websocket -> Redwood streaming endpoint with model redwood-alpha-4-l3.

Thanks,
Mark
Mark Chen
Director of Product
PulseAI

Attachments:
- svc-log-snippets.txt (text)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@pulseai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:24:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Hi Mark — thanks for flags and the logs. We see the request IDs in our ingestion traces and are investigating.

Immediate actions for quick mitigation while we triage:
- Switch to the polling (non-streaming) endpoint for critical flows until we stabilize. This is the fastest way to avoid partial-chunk stalls.
- If you must stay on streaming, reduce client chunk size to 32 tokens and set client stream_timeout to 60s (currently default is 30s).
- Enable automatic fallback: if the client receives a stall for >10s, reconnect and request the remaining tokens (resume by sending last_token_id).

We've looped in Rishi and Monica from CS to coordinate a targeted rollout and to provide a temporary SLA credit if this impacts your SLAs. We'll follow up with a timeline once infra triage completes.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:45:52 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Internal notes — triage in progress. Infra team reported elevated rpc_worker_queue length for streaming routers in us-west-2 between 07:36–08:05. Related infra alert: INF-1129.

Initial theory: a shard experienced transient backpressure triggered by a traffic spike + autoscaler lag. We've asked infra to: 1) drain affected shard, 2) temporarily route PulseAI traffic to a warm standby pool, 3) capture kernel and scheduling metrics for the period.

Action items for CS/sales:
- Monica to send customer mitigation (non-streaming fallback + client config) and confirm patched endpoints.
- Soojin to offer outbound check-in and credit if SLA crossed.
- Vivek to coordinate with infra on a permanent routing tweak (preferably avoid shard hot spots and pre-warm pools for critical customers).

I'll update here as infra posts logs.

— Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@pulseai.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:05:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Hi Mark — Monica from Customer Success. Quick update and steps we applied: 

1) Applied temporary routing so your streaming traffic is moved to an alternate warm pool (us-west-2b) — should be live now.
2) Increased per-connection read timeout on our streaming edge to 80s for your org (this reduces premature disconnects).
3) We recommend switching non-critical chat flows to the polling endpoint for the next 6 hours while infra finishes the shard drain. If you want, we can flip a feature flag from our side to force polling for specific routes.

Can you try again and let me know if latency improves? If you can send 2-3 failing request IDs after the change we'll correlate end-to-end.

Thanks — sorry for the disruption, we know this impacts your users.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@pulseai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:23:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Thanks Monica — after the routing change we're seeing a big improvement (median p95 down from ~3.2s to ~0.9s on new sessions). A couple of users still reported a 10s stall on an older websocket session; they recovered after reconnect. We'll move core flows to polling and exercise the reconnect fallback for now.

Please follow up with a short postmortem and recommended long-term fixes — we're particularly interested in: 1) whether autoscaler tuning can avoid this, 2) whether per-customer pre-warmed pools are an option, and 3) anything we should change client-side to be resilient.

-Mark

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@pulseai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live chat streaming delay - pulseAI production

Hi Mark — appreciate the verification and the data point. We're scheduling a short postmortem tomorrow (Nov 22, 10:00 PST) to review root cause and permanent mitigations. Attached is a short agenda and preliminary findings:

- What we saw: backpressure on a single streaming shard due to a traffic spike and autoscaler reaction lag; some websocket connections experienced head-of-line stalls.
- Short-term mitigations applied: routing to warm pool, increased read timeout for your org, recommendation to use polling for critical flows.
- Next steps (postmortem):
  * Infra to adjust autoscaler profiles for streaming routers (reduce cool-down, increase warm capacity).
  * Product: evaluate per-customer warm pool/route pinning for high-SLA customers.
  * SDK: add example for resumable streams + recommended client-side reconnect logic.
  * CS/Sales: prepare an SLA credit calculation and follow-up comms.

Links & artifacts: logs and heatmap (attached), internal ticket INF-1129, meeting invite (sent).

If this time doesn't work for you, tell us and we'll adjust. We'll publish a concise customer-facing postmortem after the internal review (target EOD Nov 22).

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
